correctness.rationale: Multiplying each Gompertz cause density by the competing cause survival gives a common time factor times lambda_j, so the conditional cause probability is constant in time. The source likelihood has the same factorization under its cause-neutral progressive censoring, making label placements exchangeable conditional on failure times and the cause count. Exact dynamic programming on the source's 45 printed failures gives 44,812 equally likely assignments at least as rank-extreme as observed out of 2,438,362,177,020 possibilities. The packaged checker reproduces both the analytic factorization and the integer enumeration.

originality.rationale: General proportional-hazards competing-risks literature covers the label/time separation ingredient, and a related common-shape Weibull paper explicitly gives a binomial cause count. The new content is the source-specific implication comparison: the 2026 article separately interprets cause-conditioned electrode failure-time shapes while its own common-shape model forces those distributions to coincide. The exact nuisance-free permutation diagnostic and its 1.84e-8 result were not located in the checked source, cited related paper, or targeted published-result searches.

value.rationale: The target article concludes that the Gompertz model gives a superior joint fit and presents the electrode analysis as confirmation of practical value. An exact parameter-free implication of that model is nevertheless rejected at roughly 1.84e-8 by the very failure labels and times used in the application. The result also shows why separate cause-wise fits are not checks of the latent cause marginals. This is a substantive model-diagnostic correction with direct consequences for how the application should be interpreted, not merely a rederivation of the relative-risk formula.
